crime_highlights: the complainant and her mother moved in with the applicant when she was 16 years of age and the applicant was approximately 67 years of age
the complainant was 100% dependent upon the accused for all of her needs
The applicant engaged in a sexual relationship with the complainant over a period of approximately 18 months
rationale_highlights: He is an aboriginal person who has suffered from physical and sexual abuse in his own childhood and suffers from feelings of abandonment.
His First Nations status has to be considered in light of the Gladue factors.
note: Court never states effect of Gladue factors; Charter s. 12 challenge dismissed.

crime_highlights: police seized a loaded sawed off Ruger SR-22 rifle located under the mattress of Mr. Homeniuk's bed
Both the barrel and stock of the rifle had been sawed off.
The rifle also had a live bullet in the ejection port.
At the time, Mr. Homeniuk was prohibited from possessing these items
rationale_highlights: I must and I do take judicial notice of the history of colonialization and racism as embedded systemic difficulties and social and economic depravations in Aboriginal communities

The systemic legacy of racism, colonialization and institutional discrimination is an important factor in considering an appropriate sentence, in part because it bears on the voluntariness of your actions.
A judge would err if she failed to consider the Gladue factors
note: Court says factor is important and bears on voluntariness, but may not change result.

crime_highlights: After faking the seizure AB repeatedly stated to both defendants that he wanted to go to the hospital. The defendants ignored AB's request.
Both offenders knew that AB was completely helpless
The offenders were both outside the bedroom, and heard this, but they did not accommodate his request in any way.
Mr. Eddy yelled at him in an intimidating manner.
AB was treated for abrasions to the right side of his forehead and to his lower lip.
rationale_highlights: Where applicable, Gladue factors are considered mitigating factors in sentencing
They play a substantial role in the history of Mr. Eddy's life, and the circumstances that led to the present offence.
In my view, the moral culpability of each offender is roughly equal
The Gladue factors operate to reduce Mr. Eddy's moral culpability as well as the effectiveness of imprisonment.
note: Crime passage is long (about 400 words) but only paragraph covering confinement and injuries.
